relevance_note: One decedent in this sudden-death cohort carried a LAMP2 deletion: "The third decedent with a pathogenic variant had a large ∼136 kb deletion of band q24 of chromosome X which contained part of LAMP2 gene".
method_note: Cohort study of 46 sudden-death decedents with idiopathic LVH and 125 first-degree relatives; only decedent N=36 in Table 2 (column 'N', bare numbers, hence label 'Table 2 #36') carries a LAMP2 variant, and her mother, father and brother are described in relation to her (relation words from Table 2 'Mother, 56 Father, 58 Brother, 30' and text '(mother, father, and brother)'). All other decedents and relatives are out of scope. Built by hand-written Python in scratch; every span checked verbatim by script. Relatives have no variant rows (they tested negative for the LAMP2 deletion). Relative ages are labelled by relation in the Table 2 cell, so not assigned by position; the 'Diagnosis/findings' cell 'Negative Negative Negative' is stacked and was NOT assigned by position (D-31); the relatives' exclusion of 'evidence of disease phenotype' comes from the text sentence naming mother, father and brother, which is a whole-screen negative and excludes nothing more specific (D-27), so all their checklist items stay 'not reported'. LVH, myocardial fibrosis and hypertension were not recorded for the decedent: idiopathic LVH and absence of hypertension are study inclusion/exclusion criteria (not evidence), and the absence of 'MF' in her Table 2 cell is not defined as negative. The group statement that 'none of the decedents reported premorbid cardiac symptoms' was not applied to her because the paper also says she had atrial arrhythmias before death. 'Atrial arrhythmias' was recorded as a feature but the checklist item 'supraventricular tachycardia (atrial fibrillation or flutter)' left 'not reported', because the paper does not say which atrial arrhythmia. Zygosity is not stated (female, X-linked deletion), so 'not reported'. Inheritance 'de novo' rests on both parents testing negative. The paper calls the decedents 'proband' only in general (Table 3 header, text), not this person, so is_proband is null for her. Pregnancy at 28 weeks at death was not recorded as a phenotype. The supplementary file (Table S2 with variant details) is not in the converted text, so no HGVS/coordinates are available. Contradiction: Table 2 and the Results say she 'died at rest', whereas the Discussion says she 'died suddenly in her sleep' (Table 1 treats asleep and rest as distinct modes of death); the Discussion also calls her 'the young girl' although she was 26.
